guard_streams.boundary: Programme evaluation outputs and installed-pole counts do not prove a mobile or broadband service is available, active or measured at a canonical parcel.
Evaluation design and research schedules are evidence about programme assessment, not current network coverage or performance at an address.
Application-process findings and programme governance cannot establish infrastructure deployment or service delivery at a parcel.
A research-report collection and document availability do not create parcel-level evidence or validate any coverage field.
Use-case progress and interim impact assessment do not prove public mobile coverage, indoor reception or throughput at a specific property.
Pilot-area equipment deployment does not prove which parcels are served, which networks are accessible or what performance users receive.
Competition funding, standards and strategic objectives are enablement evidence only and cannot be promoted to exact parcel coverage.
Regional use cases, private networks and connected-vehicle deployments do not prove public-network availability or quality at any parcel.
Evaluation definitions, subsidy mechanisms and voucher values do not prove build completion, orderability or delivered speed at an individual premises.
Supplier plans and subsidy eligibility inputs are forward-looking administrative evidence and cannot be treated as live parcel coverage.
Repeater legality and capability do not prove the outdoor donor signal, installed device, indoor coverage or data performance at a parcel.
A licence exemption category does not show that compliant equipment is present or that a specific property receives improved service.
Regulatory permission and testing standards cannot establish installation state, interference conditions or parcel-level signal quality.
Future regulatory deliverables and improved evidence plans are not themselves parcel coverage measurements and cannot satisfy the exact join gate.
Government ambitions, milestones and future spectrum decisions do not verify present service availability or performance for a canonical parcel.
